solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Amassed a fortune, as Oppenheimer's team did

definitions.meaning: to make a packet of money, an informal phrase for getting very rich
the Manhattan Project under Oppenheimer literally built the atomic bomb

explanation.surface: A wry comparison between getting rich and the wartime scientists at Los Alamos.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for earning a huge sum is also a literal account of building a nuclear weapon, which the Manhattan Project did.

clue.text: Island folk pursued by dangerous sea creature

indicators.note: pursued by means followed by, so the sea creature comes after the people

parts.note: folk means people, men
an orca is a killer whale

explanation.surface: Islanders chased by a killer whale.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balearic island in the Mediterranean, also spelt Minorca.

clue.text: Like indigenous houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the word sits within indigenous

explanation.surface: Something resembling native dwellings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for appreciate or enjoy, as in 'I really like that tune'.

clue.text: Flaps, performing in a role at start of show

indicators.note: performing suggests acting out, so the letters of in a role are reworked
the start of show is its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor nervously flapping when taking a part at the start of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinged surfaces on an aircraft wing that control roll are flaps.

clue.text: Maybe pensioner could drive, taking regular breaks

indicators.note: breaks at regular intervals mean every other letter of could drive is kept

explanation.surface: An elderly driver might manage at the wheel if stopping often.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an old person, of whom a pensioner is an example.

clue.text: Piano piece, opening in short musical entertainment

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the opening sits within the shortened dance
short means cut, so the last letter of the dance word goes

parts.note: ballet is a staged entertainment set to music
a gate is an opening in a fence

explanation.surface: A piano number opens a brief musical show.
explanation.definitionFit: A short light piece of music, often for piano, as Beethoven wrote.

clue.text: Be leader in fashion with Italian suit

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of fashion

explanation.surface: Advice to head the fashion world while wearing an Italian suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing beside 'fashion', but it is the verb meaning to be appropriate for.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit someone is to be fitting or proper for them, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Degree question university set in extremely simple language

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so the question and university letters go within
extremely means at the extremes, the outer letters of simple

explanation.surface: A university exam question on degree level phrased in very plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: The isolate tongue of the western Pyrenees, spoken in Spain and France.

clue.text: Unkempt beards are, if not kept in check

indicators.note: unkempt means untidy or dishevelled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scruffy beards grow if nobody trims them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes complete liberty, being unrestrained and under no control.

clue.text: Everything in trial is unbelievable in the extreme

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so everything goes into the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything said at a trial is utterly incredible.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an unbelievable one, so the superlative is unbelievable to the highest degree.

clue.text: Disturbed wild gelding

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters of gelding are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A castrated horse running wild has been upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bothered or nagged by a small worry is a mild kind of disturbance; past tense matches.

clue.text: Good question by French female, briefly a writer

parts.note: to ask is to question someone

indicators.note: a word said briefly is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: Someone poses a good question to a Frenchwoman who turns out, briefly, to be an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell was a Victorian novelist, author of Cranford and North and South.

clue.text: One sorry about daughter becoming less civil

indicators.note: about means going around, so the sorry person's word encloses the daughter's letter

parts.note: a ruer is someone who rues, regrets or is sorry

explanation.surface: An apologetic person, upset over a daughter, ends up becoming rather rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative of an adjective for impolite; less civil means more impolite.

clue.text: End of journey from foreign terminal, skirting Iran's borders

parts.note: de is French for from

indicators.note: skirting means going around, so the station word wraps round the borders

parts.note: a terminal is a station at the end of a line

indicators.note: the borders of Iran are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A foreign terminal at journey's end, with a route that skirts Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: The place one is travelling to is where the trip finishes.

clue.text: Attendants in hospital department nowadays?

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
nowadays means in our age, the present time

explanation.surface: Asking whether hospital attendants work in some modern department.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue of people who accompany and serve an important person are its attendants.

clue.text: Like a killer's single crime initially featured in magazine

indicators.note: featured in means placed within, so the weapons store holds the other letters

parts.note: an arsenal is a store of weapons, as is a magazine
single means one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of crime

explanation.surface: A single murder is written up in a crime magazine in a way that suits a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is elliptical: like a killer's weapon of choice, the poison arsenic.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a classic poisoner's weapon, so containing it is being like a murderer's dose.

clue.text: Youngster tailed by one clever old commander

indicators.note: tailed means with the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a child is a youngster
I is the Roman numeral one
arch means cunning, sly

explanation.surface: A clever child shadowed by an ancient military leader.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece, the commander of a thousand men held this rank.

clue.text: Stop limping

definitions.meaning: to stop or come to a standstill

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to cease moving and, archaically, crippled or lame in the leg.

clue.text: Amassing newfangled sources of power

indicators.note: newfangled means newly devised, so the letters of amassing are made anew

explanation.surface: Accumulating modern energy supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipes carrying fuel to homes supply energy, so they are power sources.

clue.text: Dirty farm building, with nothing moved inside

indicators.note: the letter for nothing shifts from the end of the farm building's word into its middle

parts.note: a silo is a tower on a farm for storing grain
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A grubby barn whose contents have been emptied and shuffled about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' is a verb here, to make dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirty something is to stain it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Enticed up-and-coming dandies around city

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the whole thing reads from bottom to top
around means the dandies enclose the city letters

parts.note: dudes are dandies, smart dressers
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Ambitious young dandies around town lured someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or tempt someone into something is to have seduced them.

clue.text: Repeatedly mentioning computers etc given low grading?

parts.note: IT is information technology, computers and the like
an E rating is a low grade, near the bottom of a scale

explanation.surface: Asking whether computers given a poor score keep getting mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something again and again is a matter of restating or reiterating it.

clue.text: Brass over edge of porthole on old sailing vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the cheek comes first

parts.note: brass means cheek, impudence, gall

indicators.note: here the edge is the end letter of porthole

explanation.surface: Brass fittings round a porthole on an old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the metal but means nerve; 'on' is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A large three-masted sailing ship of the Spanish treasure fleets.

clue.text: One giving needle or gas?

definitions.meaning: someone who jabs, giving an injection
gas means idle chatter, to talk rapidly

explanation.surface: Asking whether the nurse uses an injection or an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who jabs, and also a verb for chattering quickly and unintelligibly.

clue.text: Playwright having drink with performer missing start of rehearsal

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of whisky

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so that letter is removed from the performer's word

parts.note: an artist is a performer

indicators.note: the start of rehearsal is its first letter

explanation.surface: A playwright has a drink with an actor who skipped the start of rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of plays for the stage is a playwright.

clue.text: Animal, possibly from Bangkok, extinct, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the pair of words is heard rather than written

parts.note: someone from Bangkok is perhaps Thai, and extinct means gone

explanation.surface: An animal from Thailand said to have died out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid of a male tiger and a female lion is a real if rare beast.

clue.text: Gong finally sounded, interrupting dinner, say

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the letter goes inside the dinner word

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of sounded

explanation.surface: A dinner gong rings out at the end, breaking up the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' is British slang for a medal or decoration, not the dinner gong the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for an award or decoration such as an honour.

clue.text: Crampon primarily used by supple mountaineer

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of crampon

parts.note: limber means supple, flexible

explanation.surface: A lithe alpinist relies mainly on crampons.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ascends mountains is a climber; a straight synonym.

clue.text: One way to cook food, grand with pepper

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
to pepper with bullets is to riddle

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: cook it grandly, with plenty of pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pepper' is not the seasoning but the verb, as in peppering with shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook on a flat iron plate is a method of preparing food.

clue.text: Performers discovered unknown operatic intros

indicators.note: intros are introductions, the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Unknown opera singers discovered through their introductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of musicians working together, a plural noun in sense.

clue.text: One who's generous with fellow men

parts.note: a don is a college fellow at Oxford or Cambridge
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Praising someone who shares freely with other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives money or goods freely is a giver, a generous one.

clue.text: Gives to heirs with no difficulty

definitions.meaning: to pass property or traditions to the next generation
easily, as in winning without trouble

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means bequeathing to successors, and the idiom means winning very easily.
